chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, and from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah, from a man called al-Hasan, from a man he named, who said:

My father bought a sheep for me in Mina, and it was stolen. My father said to me, 'Go to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and ask him about that.' So I went to him and informed him. He said to me, 'No sheep was sacrificed in Mina that is better than your sheep.'

key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Mina (a holy site near Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling or merit of a sheep that is lost before being sacrificed during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the spiritual merit of the *dhabihah* (sacrificial animal) even before the ritual slaughter is completed, provided the intention (*niyyah*) was established. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal state of devotion over the mere physical act, suggesting that the sheep's loss in Mina was a divine test that elevated its status above those successfully sacrificed. The incident underscores the concept that sincerity in fulfilling the commandment carries its own reward, even in the face of unforeseen loss.
